claude.sample_unit: radiology reports (plus 800 patients in clinical setting validation)

links.outcome: Patient subjective and objective comprehension of LLM-simplified vs original reports
links.effect: Subjective comprehension 3.59±0.74 to 4.68±0.47; objective 1.64±0.84 to 2.78±0.42 (P<0.05); STAI-6 anxiety 16.74 to 10.44 in 800 patients
links.quote: The results of clinical setting validation showed that, compared with the original radiology reports (subjective comprehension scores: 3.59 ± 0.74；objective comprehension scores: 1.64 ± 0.84), reading the reports simplified by DeepSeek-R1 significantly improved patients’ subjective comprehension scores (4.68 ± 0.47; P < 0.05; r = 0.91；95%CI:0.89–0.92) and objective comprehension scores (2.78 ± 0.42; P < 0.05; r = 0.90；95%CI:0.88–0.91).

links.outcome: Key information point accuracy with unoptimized vs optimized structured prompts
links.effect: Accurate KIP: ChatGPT-4.0 52.2% to 86.1%; DeepSeek-R1 61.7% to 91.1%; Grok-3 99.4% to 100%
links.quote: Using the optimized prompt framework, quantitative results showed that the optimized prompts significantly improved the translation accuracy of ChatGPT-4.0 and Deep Seek-R1, as evidenced by higher key information point (KIP) retention rates (Table 5 ).

links.outcome: Output consistency across 10 repeated runs of same report
links.effect: With unoptimized prompts, accurate KIP rates were 52.2% (ChatGPT-4.0), 61.7% (DeepSeek-R1), 99.4% (Grok-3) across repeated outputs
links.quote: The variability within the same model’s response to identical inputs highlights the inherent randomness of LLMs, which contributes to output inconsistency.

links.outcome: Radiologist-identified omissions and inaccuracies in LLM-simplified reports
links.effect: Omissions per report: ChatGPT 0.072, Grok 0.047, DeepSeek 0.093; inaccuracies 0.038, 0.069, 0.05
links.quote: The findings show that these translations regularly include information omissions and inaccuracies.

links.outcome: Comprehension of LLM-simplified reports by age and education level
links.effect: Significant age × education interaction on subjective and objective comprehension (P<0.05); lower education associated with lower comprehension
links.quote: The results of the second-stage 2 × 2 factorial analysis (age × educational level) demonstrated that age and educational level had significant interactive effects on both subjective and objective comprehension scores ( P < 0.05).

openai.sample_unit: radiology reports in the retrospective stage; a subsequent standardized-report evaluation included 800 patients

links.outcome: Patient subjective and objective comprehension of simplified versus original radiology reports
links.effect: Subjective comprehension increased from 3.59 ± 0.74 to 4.68 ± 0.47; objective comprehension increased from 1.64 ± 0.84 to 2.78 ± 0.42 (both P < 0.05).
links.quote: The results of clinical setting validation showed that, compared with the original radiology reports (subjective comprehension scores: 3.59 ± 0.74；objective comprehension scores: 1.64 ± 0.84), reading the reports simplified by DeepSeek-R1 significantly improved patients’ subjective comprehension scores (4.68 ± 0.47; P < 0.05; r = 0.91；95%CI:0.89–0.92) and objective comprehension scores (2.78 ± 0.42; P < 0.05; r = 0.90；95%CI:0.88–0.91).

links.outcome: Omissions and inaccuracies in AI-generated patient-centric radiology reports
links.effect: Mean omissions/inaccuracies per report were 0.072/0.038 for ChatGPT, 0.047/0.069 for Grok, and 0.093/0.05 for Deep Seek.
links.quote: For example, translations by ChatGPT-4.0 had an average of 0.072 omissions and 0.038 inaccuracies per report, which means roughly one omission every 13.8 reports and one inaccuracy every 26.3 reports.

links.outcome: Output consistency and key-information accuracy across repeated identical inputs
links.effect: Ten outputs per model for one chest CT report showed inconsistency. Across 18 key information points, unoptimized-prompt accuracy was 52.2% for ChatGPT-4.0, 99.4% for Grok-3, and 61.7% for Deep Seek.
links.quote: The variability within the same model’s response to identical inputs highlights the inherent randomness of LLMs, which contributes to output inconsistency.

links.outcome: Key-information retention with detailed optimized versus generic prompts
links.effect: Optimized prompts increased KIP accuracy from 52.2% to 86.1% for ChatGPT-4.0, 61.7% to 91.1% for Deep Seek, and 99.4% to 100% for Grok-3; testing used one chest CT report.
links.quote: Using the optimized prompt framework, quantitative results showed that the optimized prompts significantly improved the translation accuracy of ChatGPT-4.0 and Deep Seek-R1, as evidenced by higher key information point (KIP) retention rates (Table 5 ).

links.outcome: Age- and education-related differences in comprehension of AI-simplified reports
links.effect: Older participants had better comprehension within both educational strata: Cliff’s |Δ| = 0.32 for high education and 0.41 for low education; adjusted P < 0.05.
links.quote: Results indicated significant differences: younger and older participants differed notably in understanding the reports, with older participants showing better comprehension than younger, both in high-education groups (Group 1 vs. Group 3；effect size Cliff’s |Δ| = 0.32; 95% CI: 0.21, 0.39) and low-education groups (Group 2 vs. Group 4；effect size Cliff’s |Δ| = 0.41; 95% CI: 0.32, 0.53) (adjusted P < 0.05 after Bonferroni correction; Fig. 2c, d ).

links.outcome: Output consistency across repeated runs
links.effect: Repeated generations for the same report showed variability, highlighting the inherent randomness and inconsistency of the LLMs.
links.quote: The variability within the same model’s response to identical inputs highlights the inherent randomness of LLMs, which contributes to output inconsistency.

links.outcome: Report omissions and inaccuracies
links.effect: ChatGPT-4.0 translations had an average of 0.072 omissions and 0.038 inaccuracies per report.
links.quote: For example, translations by ChatGPT-4.0 had an average of 0.072 omissions and 0.038 inaccuracies per report, which means roughly one omission every 13.8 reports and one inaccuracy every 26.3 reports.

links.outcome: Subjective and objective comprehension
links.effect: Reading reports simplified by DeepSeek-R1 significantly improved patients' subjective (4.68 vs 3.59) and objective (2.78 vs 1.64) comprehension scores.
links.quote: The results of clinical setting validation showed that, compared with the original radiology reports (subjective comprehension scores: 3.59 ± 0.74；objective comprehension scores: 1.64 ± 0.84), reading the reports simplified by DeepSeek-R1 significantly improved patients’ subjective comprehension scores (4.68 ± 0.47; P < 0.05; r = 0.91；95%CI:0.89–0.92) and objective comprehension scores (2.78 ± 0.42; P < 0.05; r = 0.90；95%CI:0.88–0.91).

links.outcome: Comprehension by age and education
links.effect: Younger and older participants differed notably in understanding the reports, with older participants demonstrating better comprehension than younger participants in both educational strata.
links.quote: Results indicated significant differences: younger and older participants differed notably in understanding the reports, with older participants showing better comprehension than younger, both in high-education groups (Group 1 vs. Group 3；effect size Cliff’s |Δ| = 0.32; 95% CI: 0.21, 0.39) and low-education groups (Group 2 vs. Group 4；effect size Cliff’s |Δ| = 0.41; 95% CI: 0.32, 0.53) (adjusted P < 0.05 after Bonferroni correction; Fig. 2c, d).

links.outcome: Translation accuracy with optimized prompts
links.effect: Optimized prompts significantly improved translation accuracy of ChatGPT-4.0 and Deep Seek-R1, resulting in higher key information point retention rates.
links.quote: Using the optimized prompt framework, quantitative results showed that the optimized prompts significantly improved the translation accuracy of ChatGPT-4.0 and Deep Seek-R1, as evidenced by higher key information point (KIP) retention rates (Table 5).

screen.practice: LLM-simplified patient-facing radiology reports (reading-level simplification) versus original reports
screen.reason: Empirical study testing the generation of simplified patient-centered radiology reports using LLMs, evaluated retrospectively and in a clinical setting with 800 patients measuring comprehension and anxiety.
